title: Customer pilot plan: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode
creator: Lauren Bishop
project: Autoscaling policies with customer bounds (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
## Summary
Run a controlled customer pilot for Dedicated autoscaling *min/max bounds* and *predictive mode* to validate semantics, reliability guardrails, and customer experience (Console/API + support workflows) before GA.

This ticket defines:
- Candidate pilot accounts + enrollment criteria
- Success criteria and stop/rollback criteria
- Comms cadence + ownership (Product/Eng/SRE/CS)
- Feedback collection process + how feedback feeds back into requirements/bugs

## Pilot goals
1) Confirm customer-configurable bounds are hard-enforced and auditable.
2) Validate predictive mode improves ramp performance (lower queue/latency) without introducing oscillation.
3) Prove on-call readiness: alerts, dashboards, and runbooks are actionable.
4) Validate customer-facing UX/semantics (Console + API) and support playbooks.

## Pilot scope
### Feature flags / enablement
- Per-account/per-deployment feature flag gate (dependency: ENG-22148)
- Pilot enablement limited to 1 region per customer initially (us-east-1 unless customer requires otherwise)
- Predictive mode defaults OFF unless explicitly requested + approved

### Included functionality
- Scaling policy fields: min_replicas, max_replicas, cooldowns, predictive_mode toggle
- Deterministic evaluation and audit trail (requested desired vs bounded desired + reason)
- Metrics/dashboards for: desired vs bounded, bound-hit rate, queue depth, saturation, prediction error

### Exclusions (pilot)
- No cross-region predictive placement optimization
- No contract renegotiation workflow automation
- No automated procurement based on forecasts

## Candidate pilot accounts (proposed)
### Tier 0 (bounds-only first; lowest risk)
1) Polaris Analytics (Dedicated POC)
   - Primary need: baseline capacity + hard cap for spend
   - Pilot ask: bounds enforcement + audit log visibility
   - Start with: bounds-only (predictive OFF)
   - Region: us-east-1

2) Lumen Legaltech (compliance-heavy)
   - Primary need: auditability of scaling config changes (who/when/what) + deterministic behavior
   - Pilot ask: bounds + audit events + export story
   - Start with: bounds-only (predictive OFF)
   - Region: us-east-1

### Tier 1 (bounds + predictive; ramp patterns)
3) Hexagon Support Systems (enterprise)
   - Pattern: predictable daily ramp; prior tickets on queueing
   - Pilot ask: predictive mode with conservative lead time; reactive override safety
   - Start with: bounds ON; predictive ON after 1 week stable
   - Region: us-east-1

4) Northstar Fintech (strict cost ceilings)
   - Pattern: known campaign/event spikes; very sensitive to max bound enforcement
   - Pilot ask: predictive mode (scheduled events) + strict max; wants proof it never exceeds cap
   - Start with: bounds ON; predictive ON after readiness review
   - Region: us-east-1

## Enrollment criteria (must-have)
- Dedicated deployment with stable baseline traffic (or known ramp schedule)
- Customer agrees to:
  - Provide expected ramp times (timezone + schedule)
  - Participate in weekly review (30 min)
  - Allow Redwood to collect/inspect anonymized performance metrics for the deployment
- Internal readiness:
  - Runbook published and reviewed (SRE)
  - Alerts installed and tested in pilot region
  - Feature flags verified + rollback path validated

## Pilot rollout plan (phased)
### Phase A: internal + canary (1 week)
- Enable in 1 internal/staging dedicated environment + perf-canary scenarios
- Validate dashboards populate; ensure no high-cardinality label issues
- Verify audit event emission and retention in logging pipeline

### Phase B: Tier 0 customers (bounds-only) (1 week)
- Enable bounds-only for Polaris + Lumen
- Validate:
  - Bounds clamp behavior (never exceed max; never drop below min)
  - Console/API semantics are understood by customer admins
  - Audit logs show config updates and autoscaler decision reasons

### Phase C: Tier 1 customers (predictive mode) (2–3 weeks)
- Enable bounds for Hexagon + Northstar
- Turn predictive ON with conservative parameters:
  - minimum lead time: 10–15 minutes
  - cooldown: >= 10 minutes
  - reactive override allowed when queue depth / saturation triggers
- Monitor closely during known ramps; rollback predictive only (keep bounds)

### Phase D: expand pilot set (optional) (1–2 weeks)
- Add 1–2 additional Dedicated customers if Phase C is stable and SRE approves

## Success criteria (pilot)
### Functional correctness
- Hard invariants observed:
  - 0 instances of max bound exceeded
  - 0 instances of scale-down below min (except explicit customer action to lower min)
- Determinism/auditability:
  - For each scale event, we can answer: requested desired, bounded desired, and reason

### Reliability / performance
- Bounds-only customers:
  - No regression in p95 latency during steady state vs pre-pilot baseline
  - Bound-hit rate is visible and interpretable (customer + on-call)

- Predictive mode customers (during scheduled ramps):
  - Reduce queue depth at ramp start by >= 30% compared to reactive-only baseline (or equivalent “time to drain queue” improvement)
  - No sustained oscillation (defined as >3 scale direction changes within 30 minutes not driven by real traffic changes)
  - p95 latency during ramp improves or is flat (no regression >5%)

### Operability
- Alerts:
  - Max-bound saturation alert fires when expected; paging is not noisy (>2 pages/week/customer is considered too noisy)
- Runbook:
  - On-call can diagnose within 15 minutes whether issue is: max cap, min unmet (capacity shortage), predictive pipeline stale, or reactive signal spike

### Customer experience
- Customer can explain in their own words:
  - What min/max does
  - What predictive mode changes
  - What they should do when they hit max (raise cap vs optimize vs change traffic expectations)
- Support can handle 80% of inbound questions using the escalation playbook without engineering intervention

## Stop criteria / rollback rules
- Any incident where max bound is exceeded => immediate pilot pause, incident review, block expansion until fixed
- If predictive causes oscillation impacting latency for >30 minutes => disable predictive for that deployment (bounds remain)
- If region capacity shortage prevents meeting min for >60 minutes:
  - Flag deployment as degraded; notify CS + customer; evaluate moving baseline to alternate region only if contract allows (out of scope for pilot feature; handled case-by-case)

## Comms plan
### Internal
- Slack channel: #dedicated-autoscaling-pilot (create/confirm)
- Weekly internal pilot sync (30 min): Product (Lauren), Eng (Vanessa/Ethan), SRE (Rafael), Observability (Allison), CS (Rachel/Miguel)
- Daily async updates during predictive ramp windows (Phase C) posted by pilot coordinator (Miguel)

### Customer
- Kickoff email (owner: TAM Liam O’Rourke + Rachel Kim):
  - Scope + expectations
  - How to request config changes
  - How to interpret “bounded” state and what the cap implies
- Cadence:
  - Week 0: kickoff + enablement
  - Week 1–3: weekly 30-min review (graphs + bound-hit + latency)
  - Incident comms: same-day update + follow-up summary within 48h

## Feedback collection process
- Single source of truth: shared pilot notes doc (owner: Talia) with per-customer sections
- Tagging:
  - All issues/asks filed to Linear with label “Customer Pilot” + customer name
  - Support tickets tagged with “autoscaling-bounds-pilot” and linked back here
- Data to review weekly:
  - Bound-hit rate and times of day
  - Queue depth, saturation, scale event timeline
  - Prediction vs actual demand; staleness events
  - Qualitative notes: customer confidence, config comprehension, desired UX improvements

## Pilot deliverables
- Per-customer enablement checklist completed and linked (flags, region, config, contacts)
- Weekly pilot summary posted internally (wins, issues, next actions)
- End-of-pilot report:
  - Metrics vs success criteria
  - List of changes required for GA
  - GA recommendation (go/no-go) with risks

## Owners
- Pilot execution: Talia Benson
- Customer coordination + scheduling: Miguel Santos (CS) + Liam O’Rourke (TAM)
- Engineering escalation: Vanessa Ortiz (autoscaler), Ethan Park (control plane)
- SRE readiness + on-call: Rafael Mendes
- Observability: Allison Grant

## Open questions
1) Do we require predictive mode to be opt-in per deployment (not just per account)? (recommend YES)
2) Do we provide “recommended range” hints in Console during pilot or keep it internal? (recommend: internal guidance only; avoid confusing early semantics)
3) What’s the minimum history required before enabling predictive? (tentative: >= 7 days or explicit scheduled events)
